Title: Diagnosis of test `testLang412Left`
Details: The test `testLang412Left` creates an instance of `StrBuilder` and calls `appendFixedWidthPadLeft` with a `null` object, width 10, and pad character '*'.

Looking at the method `appendFixedWidthPadLeft(Object obj, int width, char padChar)`, when the object is `null`, the code assigns `str` as `getNullText()`. This method returns the value of the `nullText` field in `StrBuilder`. If `nullText` is not set, it may be `null`.

Then, the code does `int strLen = str.length();`. If `str` is `null` (which happens if `getNullText()` returns `null`), this causes a `NullPointerException`. This suggests that the test fails because `nullText` has not been initialized and is `null`, causing the crash when calling `length()` on it.

The method `setNullText(String nullText)` sets this `nullText` field, with logic to convert empty strings to `null`. But if no `nullText` was set before calling `appendFixedWidthPadLeft`, it remains `null`.

Hence, the bug occurs due to the failure to handle the case where `nullText` is `null` in `appendFixedWidthPadLeft`. The method assumes `str` will never be `null`, which is wrong.

To fix the bug, either `appendFixedWidthPadLeft` should provide a default string when `getNullText()` returns `null`, or the class invariants should ensure `nullText` is never `null` before this method is called.

Suggested locations to fix:
- `StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadLeft(Object, int, char)`
